title: What to watch at the open
text: A big week starts today, and stock futures were pointing lower this morning, led by AI stocks. Futures are bets on where prices will open. The main event is NVIDIA's earnings report on Tuesday after the market closes. On Wednesday the Federal Reserve shares notes from its last meeting, and later this week Anthropic, an AI company, plans to start selling shares to the public. Our prices below are from Friday's close, so expect them to move once trading begins at 9:30 am New York time.

title: NVIDIA reports on Tuesday
text: NVIDIA will share its results for the three months that ended October 25 on Tuesday, right after the market closes. It is the first report since its leadership change. NVIDIA closed Friday at $162.85, only 15% of the way up its one year range and about 9% above its one year low of $148.80. Analysts' average target is $317.87, but targets are guesses and can change after a report. Many chip stocks on our list, like AMD, Broadcom, TSMC and Vertiv, often move when NVIDIA reports.

title: Fed meeting notes come out Wednesday
text: The Federal Reserve will publish the minutes, which are the written notes, from its October meeting on Wednesday at 2 pm New York time. Last week a report showed wholesale prices up 6.5% from a year ago, and traders started to expect a rate hike in December. The notes may show how worried Fed leaders are about prices. Higher rates can make fast growing stocks less attractive. The 10 year Treasury yield averaged 5.13% in October, its highest monthly level in our chart.

title: A giant AI company may go public this week
text: Anthropic has set a price range of $70 to $78 per share for its first public sale of stock, with a planned listing on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. If it sells at those prices, it would be one of the biggest stock debuts ever. Amazon and Alphabet own stakes in Anthropic, so the price it gets could affect how investors view those two companies too. A big new stock can also pull money away from other AI stocks for a few days.

title: Lesson 52: What is an IPO?
text: IPO stands for initial public offering. It is the first time a private company sells its shares to the public on a stock exchange. Before an IPO, only founders, workers and a few big investors can own the company. Think of a lemonade stand that has grown big: to raise money for more stands, the owners let anyone buy a small piece of the business. The company and its bankers pick a price range first, then set a final price the night before trading starts. On the first day the price can jump or drop a lot, because nobody knows yet what the market thinks it is worth. That is why many careful investors wait a while before buying a new stock.
